title.narrative: Bridging the Learning Gap: Holistic Education Support for Crisis-Affected Children in Gumi Eldalo Woreda of East Borana and Saba Boru Woreda of Guji Zones.

description.narrative: ltpgtGayo Pastoral Development Initiative (GPDI), in collaboration with sub implementing partner Oromia Development Association (ODA), is proposing a vital emergency education project in Gumi Eldalo (East Borena zone) and Saba Boru (Guji zone) Woredas of Oromia regional state. This initiative is designed to address the severe educational disruption faced by communities struggling with the dual crises of armed conflict and recurrent drought. Both Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and host communities will benefit from targeted educational interventions.ltbrgtAn April 2025 GPDI assessment and data gathered during the project development revealed that there are over 400,000 displaced individuals across the East Borena and Guji zones due to the armed conflict. These populations, along with host communities, are experiencing critical food shortages resulting from successive failed rainy seasons, livestock decline, and widespread water scarcity due to insufficient pond water capture and non-functional water schemes.ltbrgtThe prolonged humanitarian crisis has devastated essential services, including education. Schools have been damaged, closed, or become inaccessible due to insecurity, forcing families to prioritize basic survival over their children's schooling. This crisis has disproportionately affected school-aged children, leaving them vulnerable to prolonged educational disruption, exploitation, and long-term psychosocial impacts. Existing formal education structures are often inadequate or non-existent/damaged in these areas, highlighting the urgent need for flexible, alternative learning solutions that also address children's holistic well-being.ltbrgtThis project aims to reach 20,570 individuals through comprehensive accelerated education programs. It will employ an inclusive strategy, actively mainstreaming protection, Gender-Based Violence (GBV) prevention, and Accountability to Affected People (AAP) throughout all interventions. Key protection outcomes include strengthening case management for at-risk children, GBV survivors, and other vulnerable children, alongside establishing functional referral pathways across all target Woredas.ltbrgtAligned with the Education Cluster's priorities, the project will implement a multi-layered approach to maximize efficiency. Core activities will focus on:ltbrgt Provision of non-formal education: Offering flexible learning opportunities outside traditional school settings.ltbrgt Home/community-based education: Bringing education directly to children within their communities.ltbrgt Distribution of teaching and learning materials: Ensuring children have the necessary resources for their education.ltbrgt Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) and Social and Emotional Learning (SEL): Addressing the psychological well-being of children affected by trauma and displacement.ltbrgt Inclusive education: Prioritizing access and support for all children, regardless of their background or circumstances.ltbrgtThis project represents a crucial step in providing essential educational opportunities and safeguarding the future of children in these highly vulnerable communities.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
